newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican prosecutor in hiding says wants justice.
newsitem.headline: Mexican prosecutor in hiding says wants justice.

text.p: A former Mexican government prosecutor now in hiding pleaded on Wednesday to be judged according to the law and not for political reasons in a case involving the jailed brother of a former president.

In an open letter published in Mexico City newspapers on Wednesday, Pablo Chapa Bezanilla said he was ready to appear to answer charges he paid $450,000 to witnesses in a complicated case involving a skeleton, a witch and Raul Salinas, brother of the former president.
Chapa demanded in the letter, written from "somewhere in Mexico," that observers from a human rights organisation be present during any questioning.
Chapa has been on the run since being accused of making illegal payments to witnesses in the probe of the Sept. 28, 1994 assassination of ruling party leader Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.

Officials originally charged that a skeleton dug up at a ranch used by former President Carlos Salinas's brother Raul was likely that of a missing legislator believed to have been killed because of his part in the Ruiz murder.
Raul Salinas is in jail on charges of planning the Ruiz murder and authorities were trying to pin the suspected murder of the legislator on him as well.
The skeleton turned out to have been planted by a witch and soothsayer who was helping Chapa in the case, authorities later charged.
DNA testing showed it was not the missing man but in fact a relative of the witch whose body she and other relatives stole from a cemetery and reburied at the ranch.
The witch has been charged with body-snatching and grave-robbing, while Chapa is on the run from justice over allegations that he paid witnesses in the case.
